title: Attack, Spell, Hit, and Damage over Time Tags in Path of Exile 2
shortTitle: Attack vs Spell vs Hit vs DoT
summary: Clear up the four most confused skill concepts in Path of Exile 2: Attack, Spell, Hit, and Damage over Time. Learn which modifiers apply to which skills and how behaviour tags work.
description: A concise Path of Exile 2 mechanics guide explaining the difference between Attack and Spell (skill category), Hit and Damage over Time (damage form), and behaviour tags such as Projectile, AoE, Melee, Duration, Minion, and Totem. Includes a modifier-compatibility diagnostic and worked examples.
imageAlt: A Path of Exile 2 skill icon illustrating the difference between attack, spell, hit and damage over time skill tags
prerequisites: Basic understanding of the Path of Exile 2 skill gem and support gem system
Familiarity with reading a skill tooltip and its listed tags
Awareness that damage has types (Physical, Fire, Cold, Lightning, Chaos)
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team

items.title: What is an Attack?
body: An Attack is a skill that directly uses your equipped weapon to damage enemies. Attacks can deal any damage type and usually roll a hit against the target's evasion using your Accuracy.

items.title: What is a Spell?
body: A Spell is a skill that uses raw magic rather than a weapon. Spells are not Attacks, they ignore Accuracy and evasion, and their base damage and critical chance come from the skill itself.

items.title: What is a Hit?
body: A Hit is a single, discrete instance of damage dealt at a moment in time. Most Attacks and Spells deal damage as Hits, and Hits can crit, leech, and trigger on-hit effects.

items.title: What is Damage over Time?
body: Damage over Time (DoT) is damage applied gradually across a duration instead of all at once. DoT is not a Hit, so it normally cannot crit, leech, or trigger on-hit effects the way a Hit does.

sections.title: Key terms
paragraphs: Four different concepts get tangled together when players talk about 'tags'. They answer different questions and are mostly independent of one another.

Skill Type (Attack vs Spell) answers how the skill is delivered. Damage Type (Physical, Fire, Cold, Lightning, Chaos) answers what element or form the damage is. Hit Type answers whether the damage arrives as a single Hit or as Damage over Time. Behaviour Tags (Projectile, AoE, Melee, Duration, Minion, Totem) answer how the skill is delivered or who owns it. None of these four layers determines another by itself.
bullets: Skill Type: Attack (uses a weapon) or Spell (uses magic). This is the skill's category.
Damage Type: Physical, Fire, Cold, Lightning, or Chaos. Any skill type can deal any damage type.
Hit Type: a Hit (instant) or Damage over Time (gradual). Ailments such as Ignite and Poison are forms of DoT.
Behaviour Tag: Projectile, AoE, Melee, Duration, Minion, Totem. These describe delivery and ownership, not damage type.

sections.title: Skill category relationship map
sections.caption: How the Attack and Spell categories relate to damage type, accuracy, and hit status. Skill type and damage type are orthogonal.
sections.note: A Spell can deal Fire, Cold, Lightning, or Chaos; an Attack can deal Fire (for example with a converted or elemental weapon). The category never fixes the damage type.

sections.title: Hit vs Damage over Time
sections.caption: How different damage forms behave in Path of Exile 2. Based on the PoE2 wiki: Damage over Time is not a Hit, so it is unaffected by penetration, and resistances still mitigate it.

cells.can-leech: Yes (per recovery mechanics in 0.5.4, pending PC verification)

cells.can-crit: No - ailments do not crit by default

cells.affected-by-penetration: No - penetration only applies to hits

sections.note: Resistances in the matching damage type still mitigate DoT, but armour and penetration do not, because those only apply to Hits. Recovery (Leech) behaviour is version-sensitive in 0.5.4 and flagged for PC confirmation.

sections.title: What behaviour tags do and do not imply
paragraphs: Behaviour tags describe how a skill is delivered or who owns it. They are separate from both Skill Type and Damage Type. A tag such as Projectile tells you the skill fires a projectile; it does not tell you whether the skill is an Attack or a Spell, nor what damage type it deals.

The same is true for AoE, Melee, Duration, Minion, and Totem. A Minion skill is cast by your minion, a Totem skill is cast by a totem you place, and a Duration skill persists for a time - none of these fix the damage type or the Attack/Spell category.
bullets: Projectile: the skill travels as a projectile. It can be an Attack (Bow shot) or a Spell (a spell projectile).
AoE: deals damage in an area. Applies to both Attacks and Spells.
Melee: delivered at close range. Almost always an Attack, but the tag alone does not set the damage type.
Duration: the effect lasts for a duration (for example a ground effect or aura). Not a Hit by itself.
Minion / Totem: describe ownership of the skill, not its damage type. Support-gem compatibility still depends on the underlying skill tags.

sections.title: Modifier compatibility diagnostic
sections.intro: Use this to check whether a damage modifier or support gem will apply to your skill. Pick your skill type, then the modifier scope.

controls.label: What does the modifier or support say?

rules.title: Attack Damage applies
steps: The modifier or support targets Attack Damage.
Your skill is an Attack, so it receives the bonus.

rules.title: Spell Damage applies
steps: The modifier or support targets Spell Damage.
Your skill is a Spell, so it receives the bonus.

rules.title: Projectile Damage - check the tag
steps: It applies only if your Attack also has the Projectile tag (for example a Bow or Crossbow skill).

rules.title: Projectile Damage on a Spell - check the tag
steps: It applies only if your Spell also has the Projectile tag (for example a spell that fires a projectile).

rules.title: Mismatch - Attack Damage on a Spell
steps: Attack Damage modifiers do not apply to Spells.
A support gem with the Attack tag will show as incompatible on a Spell skill.

rules.title: Mismatch - Spell Damage on an Attack
steps: Spell Damage modifiers do not apply to Attacks.
A support gem with the Spell tag will show as incompatible on an Attack skill.

rules.title: Generic Damage applies
steps: Generic Damage or Elemental Damage modifiers apply to any skill regardless of category.
They still must match the damage type (for example Fire Damage only helps Fire skills).

rules.title: Generic Damage applies
steps: Generic Damage or Elemental Damage modifiers apply to any skill regardless of category.
They still must match the damage type (for example Cold Damage only helps Cold skills).

defaultResult.title: Still unsure?
steps: Read the exact wording on the modifier or support gem.
Match the category word (Attack / Spell / Projectile) to your skill's tags.
If the tag is missing, the modifier will not apply and the support may show as incompatible.

sections.title: Worked examples
sections.caption: Four common builds showing skill type, tags, and which damage modifiers apply. This is illustrative, not exhaustive.

cells.skill: A Bow skill dealing physical damage
cells.what-applies: Attack Damage, Projectile Damage, and Physical Damage modifiers all apply. Evasion matters for the hit.

cells.skill: A weapon attack converted to Fire
cells.what-applies: Attack Damage and Fire Damage modifiers apply. Spell Damage does not. Penetration affects the hit.
Spell Damage and Cold Damage modifiers apply. Attack Damage does not. Accuracy is irrelevant.

cells.skill: An ailment dealing Damage over Time
cells.what-applies: DoT and ailment multipliers apply. It is not a Hit, so crit, leech, on-hit, and penetration do not apply the same way. Resistance still mitigates.

sections.note: Exact modifier names vary by patch. Always read the skill tooltip tags and the modifier wording in game.

sections.title: Common misreads
paragraphs: Most build mistakes around these tags come from assuming one layer controls another. Watch for the traps below.
bullets: Assuming an Attack is always Physical - Attacks can deal Fire, Cold, Lightning, or Chaos.
Assuming a Spell cannot deal Physical - Spell base damage is set by the skill, not the weapon, but the damage type is still independent.
Adding Attack Damage to a Spell, or Spell Damage to an Attack - the bonus simply will not apply.
Expecting a DoT or ailment to crit, leech, or trigger on-hit effects - these are not Hits.
Expecting penetration to help a DoT - penetration only applies to Hits; use exposure or ailment magnitude instead.
Reading a Projectile or Minion tag as a damage-type signal - it only describes delivery or ownership.

sections.title: Common player confusions
sections.intro: Paraphrased confusions players frequently raise about skill tags in Path of Exile 2.

cards.title: My spell did no damage from Attack support
body: A Spell skill with no Attack tag will reject Attack-type support gems. The gem shows incompatible because the category does not match.

cards.title: Why did my ignite not crit?
body: Ignite is Damage over Time, not a Hit. By default ailments do not crit and do not benefit from critical damage bonuses.

cards.title: Penetration felt useless on poison
body: Poison is a DoT. Penetration only applies to Hits, so it does not help the damage-over-time portion. Resistance still reduces it.

cards.title: Minion skill ignored my spell gems
body: Minion describes who casts the skill. Whether spell supports apply depends on the minion skill's own tags, which are version-sensitive - confirm in game.

timestamps.label: Which modifiers apply to which skills

items.question: Is an Attack always Physical damage?
answer: No. An Attack is a skill category defined by using your weapon. Attacks can deal Physical, Fire, Cold, Lightning, or Chaos damage. The damage type is independent of the Attack/Spell category.

items.question: Does a Spell use Accuracy or hit chance?
answer: No. Spells are not affected by Accuracy or evasion. Their base damage, cast speed, and critical chance come from the skill itself, not from a weapon.

items.question: Is Damage over Time a Hit?
answer: No. Damage over Time is applied gradually across a duration and does not count as a Hit. Because of that, bonuses and defences that apply to hits (such as penetration and armour) do not affect it, while resistance in the matching damage type still mitigates it.

items.question: Can Damage over Time crit or leech?
answer: By default, Damage over Time and ailments such as Ignite, Bleed, and Poison do not crit and do not trigger on-hit effects. Whether they can leech depends on the current recovery mechanics in 0.5.4 and is flagged for PC confirmation.

items.question: Do behaviour tags like Projectile or Minion set the damage type?
answer: No. Projectile, AoE, Melee, Duration, Minion, and Totem describe how a skill is delivered or who owns it. They do not determine whether the skill is an Attack or a Spell, nor what damage type it deals.

items.question: Why does my support gem show as incompatible?
answer: A support gem only applies if its required tags match the skill's tags. A gem requiring the Attack tag will not slot into a Spell, and one requiring Spell will not slot into an Attack. Read both the skill and the support tooltip tags.
